column1: # IpTunnel network-settings validator parity table, v1.
# ONE physical table, read by BOTH validators:
# THE TWO ARE NOT SYMMETRIC PEERS. Rust is strictly stricter: every rule Swift
# holds, Rust also holds, and Rust adds session-id trim/charset rules plus
# equality against the auth TunnelAck. `swift_only` is therefore EMPTY — and it
# is kept, declared, and parsed anyway, because an empty set is an executable
# assertion that Swift has acquired no rule of its own. The day Swift gains one,
# this category stops being empty and the parity claim must be revisited.
#   both       rules genuinely implemented twice. `ack_*` equals `settings_*`
#              and mtu/session are valid on both sides, so only the rule under
#   rust_only  rules Swift does not hold: mtu/session equality against the ack,
#   swift_only EMPTY by measurement, not by omission.
# The unused verdict column is `n/a`; a parser MUST reject a row carrying a
# verdict for a side the row does not apply to.
# Addresses are TEST-NET-1/2/3 (RFC 5737) and literal negatives only. No
# SENTINELS — explicit and reversible, so no value depends on accidental TSV
# trimming. A parser MUST reject any other <...> token as an unknown sentinel.
#   <sp>     one space, usable anywhere in the token
# Hyphen acceptance is proven by `sess-alpha` on accepting rows; underscore is
# proven by its own row rather than assumed.
# Directives are DATA. Each side asserts the declared total, the per-category
# counts and the exact ordered id list for EVERY category — including the empty
# one — so a consumer that silently skips rows fails.
